newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fuji Heavy says no plans for higher 96/97 dividend.
newsitem.headline: Fuji Heavy says no plans for higher 96/97 dividend.

text.p: Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd said on Friday it has no plans to increase its dividend for the year ending March 31.

Business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun had said the company was likely to raise its dividend to six to seven yen per share from the five yen it paid last year because its parent current profit for the current business year is expected to triple from a year earlier to around 30 billion yen.
"The report was speculation. We don't have any plans to raise the dividend for 1996/97," a Fuji Heavy spokesman said.
In November, Fuji Heavy forecast an annual dividend of five yen for 1996/97.

Fuji Heavy, which makes Subaru brand cars, said on Wednesday it had received domestic orders for 4,000 of its new Forester light sport-utility vehicle in the first 20 days after its launch with a monthly target of 3,000.

Car industry analysts said on Wednesday that Fuji's parent current profit would be at least 28 billion yen for 1996/97, bigger than the firm's own forecast in November of 26 billion yen, mainly due to strong demand for its new sport-utility model and wagon models.
